symbolic_guard: shared inherited IO phase plus static ParamRTL port-shape validation
rationale: MorphVerilog runs the inherited IO-shape guard on the concrete witness, while ParamRTL retains a static named port direction and packed-type schema for every legal parameter value.

symbolic_guard: shared inherited hierarchy phase plus ParamRTL module dependency, mixed-local dependency, generate-scope and typed named-binding validation
rationale: MorphVerilog runs the inherited hierarchy phase on the concrete witness; ParamRTL separately validates the symbolic module graph, typed bindings, one combined local graph, bounded generate-for scope, both generate-if branches and every generate-case choice/default, while default-shape recursion substitutes bindings and recomputes mixed locals per instance.

symbolic_guard: ParamRTL symbolic expression, portable address-width, target-neutral ceiling-log2, minimum/maximum, mixed local-parameter, Boolean-expression, integer-comparison, conditional-integer, indexed-part-select, runtime-process and enabled bounded-memory and synchronous-counter type/domain proof
rationale: The concrete witness runs the shared inherited phase and the guarded frontend preserves implemented constant expressions, portable address-width expressions, target-neutral ceiling-log2 expressions and direct runtime-process/memory port references for ParamRTL proof. Bound public defaults are evaluated per instance before the combined dependency-first local graph, conditional child locals and widths are recomputed. ParamRTL proves CeilLog2 and AddressWidth have positive operand domains; CeilLog2 preserves the mathematical zero at operand one, while AddressWidth returns at least one and remains correlated with memory depth. Strict Verilog-2001 target capability separately enforces the positive signed-32-bit operand ceiling, then emits one module-local morphhdl$ceil_log2 constant function per consuming module with backend-internal minimum zero or one. The helper renders each operand once and creates no runtime hardware. Min/Max alone retain their 4096-node ternary expansion cap and compute conservative exact bounds before canonical lowering. Combinational conditions and sequential clock/reset/enable controls are exact unsigned one-bit inputs; memory clock/read-enable/write-enable roles are likewise distinct exact unsigned one-bit inputs, while runtime and memory data paths are exactly type-compatible with their targets for the complete legal width domain. Conditional intervals conservatively hull both branches without guard correlation; broader general runtime expressions remain planned. Increment 25 additionally ties a direct positive public counter limit to the exact unsigned AddressWidth(limit) state output over the complete finite legal domain.

symbolic_guard: predicate-aware ParamRTL driver and bounded process/memory/counter coverage
rationale: The concrete witness runs the inherited phase and ParamRTL proves exact output coverage for canonical generate-for, generate-if and generate-case configurations, both paths of one complete CombinationalIf, sole ownership by each atomic register variant and sole read-output/memory ownership for the bounded memory, including intentional disabled-read hold. Each enabled register's absent disabled assignment is intentional sequential hold; the memory's disabled read is intentional sequential hold and its unwritten content is explicit unspecified state, not an incomplete combinational driver. Mixed procedural/structural drivers fail before emission; general expressions, multiple or nested runtime statements and broader sequential/memory forms keep the guard partial. The atomic counter solely owns its output; its absent disabled assignment is intentional sequential hold and its reset, terminal-wrap and increment paths are complete.

symbolic_guard: atomic ParamRTL register, counter and synchronous-memory completeness/ownership proof
rationale: Increments 16 through 19 admit atomic rising-edge registers only when the sole output has a complete reset/capture/hold policy. Increments 20 through 22 define one atomic synchronous memory whose read output updates on every enabled edge and intentionally holds while read enable is low, whose optional write is an independent storage update, and whose surplus address has a complete enabled-zero/no-write policy. No sibling process, hierarchy, generate or continuous driver is allowed. General clocked statements, arbitrary hold values, multiple registers and broader memory/process coverage remain unimplemented, so the disposition stays partial. Increment 25 adds one atomic counter with complete reset/wrap/increment/hold policy and sole output ownership.

symbolic_guard: shared graph check plus symbolic generate analysis
rationale: The Increment 15 direct input-to-output combinational process and Increment 16 through 19 direct input-to-register-output processes cannot encode a combinational feedback edge, while the inherited concrete graph guard still runs. Intentional enabled hold is state feedback, not a combinational path. General runtime expressions require a ParamRTL dependency-graph adaptation before this disposition can advance. The counter's count feedback is clocked state and cannot encode a combinational loop.

symbolic_guard: one-clock bounded process/memory/counter restriction plus shared concrete CDC check
rationale: Increments 16 through 22 each encode one validated unsigned one-bit input clock and forbid sibling processes, hierarchy and generate structure, so an internal multi-domain crossing is unrepresentable in each tranche. They do not model or approve external input-domain provenance, multiple clocks or CDC structures, so the broader CDC disposition remains partial. Increment 25 preserves this restriction for one counter and forbids sibling processes or clocks.
The shared finalizer rejects leaked DSL and clock-domain stacks after configured phase inserters; PhaseContext.doPhase independently keeps every pending phase error fatal.
